reconcile.connective: Harmonizers read the one sign as a single seal over the whole promise — healing, the added fifteen years, and the city's deliverance together — so the two accounts name parts of one referent, not rival ones.

discrepancy.connective: The objection is pressed by Steve Wells of the Skeptic's Annotated Bible, who sets the Kings account (the sign confirms the healing) against the Isaiah account (the sign confirms deliverance from Assyria) as assigning the prodigy two different purposes.

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.attribution: Steve Wells, The Skeptic's Annotated Bible, "Why did God turn the sundial back ten degrees?"

excerpts.excerpt_text: …which was a token confirming and assuring that the Lord will do this thing that he hath spoken; recover Hezekiah from his sickness, so that on the third day he should go up to the temple; have fifteen years added to his days; and the city of Jerusalem protected from the attempts of the Assyrian monarch.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly answers the differing-referent objection: Gill reads the single sign as confirming the entire promise at once (healing + the third-day temple visit + fifteen added years + deliverance of the city), so Kings and Isaiah name facets of one referent rather than two rival purposes.

pd_work.resource: John Gill, Exposition of the Entire Bible (1746-63), on Isaiah 38:6
pd_work.author: John Gill
pd_work.note: Gill treats this passage directly, reading the one sundial sign as a single token that confirms the whole promise to Hezekiah — recovery, the added fifteen years, and the protection of Jerusalem from Assyria — which is the harmonizing answer to the differing-referent charge.
